title: 800 Women in Pink Sarees, a 60-Foot Waterfall Poster, and Bollywood's Maddest Franchise Returns
excerpt: Dhamaal 4 arrives in cinemas worldwide July 10, bringing the original gang, a Gulabi Sadi remix, and the kind of promotional madness that shut down a Thane mall
body:
The poster was sixty feet tall and it came down a waterfall.

That's how you launch a Dhamaal film. Not in a hotel ballroom with a projector and a microphone, but at Imagicaa, the amusement park on Mumbai's outskirts, where the makers of Dhamaal 4 cascaded a massive poster down the park's grand waterfall with the entire cast standing beneath it. The media weren't invited to a press conference — they were invited to an experience. Rides, treasure hunts, and the kind of over-the-top energy that this franchise has turned into a business model since 2007.

And then, two weeks later, they shut down a mall.

"On June 27, Riteish Deshmukh and newcomer Anjali Anand* launched the film's latest track, Saree*, at a mall in Thane surrounded by 800 women dressed in pink sarees."**

On June 27, Riteish Deshmukh and newcomer Anjali Anand launched the film's latest track, Saree, at a mall in Thane surrounded by 800 women dressed in pink sarees. The song — a peppy Hindi remix of Sanju Rathod's viral Marathi anthem Gulabi Sadi — was always designed to be a moment, and the visual of a sea of pink silk across two floors of a shopping centre guaranteed it. Riteish and Anjali performed live, the crowd lost its mind, and whatever remained of a normal Saturday in Thane evaporated entirely.

"It'll be a spectacular visual treat for fans and the media alike." — Production source

!Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

Dhamaal 4 hits cinemas worldwide on July 10, and if the promotional campaign is any indication, director Indra Kumar has zero interest in subtlety. The fourth instalment brings back the franchise's beloved core — Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh, Jaaved Jaaferi, and Sanjay Mishra — the five-man comic engine that has powered three increasingly unhinged films about treasure hunts, road trips, and the complete annihilation of common sense. Joining them this round are Esha Gupta, Sanjeeda Shaikh, Anjali Anand, Upendra Limaye, Ravi Kishan, and Vijay Patkar — broadening the ensemble into something that resembles a small army of chaos agents.

The music is already doing heavy lifting. Guru Randhawa's Qeher, which dropped June 19, is a pure energy track designed for mass theatres and wedding playlists. Kangna, sung by Mamta Sharma — the voice behind the legendary Munni Badnaam — brings wedding vibes and deep nostalgia. And Saree, with Sanju Rathod lending his own voice to the Hindi version, has crossed cultural lines in a way that feels genuinely organic — a Marathi folk sensation reborn as a Bollywood spectacle.

The release date itself tells a story about how Bollywood's biggest names are navigating the most packed theatrical calendar in years. Dhamaal 4 was originally set for July 3 but moved after Ajay Devgn and Akshay Kumar reportedly had a direct conversation — a gentleman's agreement, essentially — that two large-scale comedies a week apart would cannibalise each other. The shift gave Welcome To The Jungle a clean opening run. Then Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey locked July 17, and the makers pivoted again to July 10, ensuring a clear week before Nolan's epic devours every IMAX and premium screen in the country.

It's savvy scheduling from a team that knows its audience. The Dhamaal franchise has never pretended to be anything other than what it is: loud, messy, unapologetically slapstick family entertainment. Total Dhamaal was a massive hit in 2019, and the fourth film arrives at a moment when the theatrical market is hungry for franchise-driven, repeat-watch comedies that keep footfall alive between the tentpole event releases.

For the diaspora, Dhamaal 4 releases day-and-date in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and the Middle East — the global footprint that's now standard for Hindi tentpoles. Whether you're in a PVR in Mumbai or a Cinemark in New Jersey, the experience is engineered to be identical: maximum volume, zero sophistication, complete surrender to the madness.

Between Welcome To The Jungle (which crossed ₹95 crore worldwide in three days), Alpha's spy-universe ambitions, and now this, Bollywood is riding the franchise wave harder than any summer in recent memory. Arshad Warsi, who is somehow in all of them, deserves a vacation after July — or at least a very good accountant.

Dhamaal 4 releases in cinemas worldwide on July 10.
